definition_title: Valuation lower bounds from weighted polynomial degree
natural_language_statement: For an additive valuation into WithTop ℝ, valuation of a finite product is the sum of the valuations of its factors. If each variable value has valuation at least −w i · D, each coefficient has nonnegative valuation, and every exponent in a multivariate polynomial’s support has w-weight at most N, then evaluating the polynomial at those variable values has valuation at least −N · D. The bundle also maps integer-valued additive valuations to real-valued ones.
explanation: The monomial estimate sums the coordinate valuation bounds with their exponents and uses the nonnegative coefficient bound. The polynomial estimate extends this to a finite sum using the valuation’s sum inequality and the support-weight hypothesis.
